title: Knowledge check: Introduction to Django's ORM

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Introduction to Django's ORM”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Object-relational mapping” under lesson 66, “Introduction to Django's ORM”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for the django orm and querysets.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Introduction to Django's ORM”?
options: Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Introduction to Django's ORM” in a real application?
options: Assume that reducing query count always makes every request faster.
Measure query behavior and verify the proposed optimization with representative data.
Add indexes to every field without checking query plans.
Materialize every database row into memory before filtering.
questions.answer_key: Measure query behavior and verify the proposed optimization with representative data.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of The Django ORM and QuerySets. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
